Ezekiel 9:1.text: He cried into my ears with a loud voice, saying, “The city’s retribution has drawn near.” Each had the implements of destruction in his hand.

Ezekiel 9:2.text: And behold, six men came from the direction of the high gate facing north, each with an axe in his hand. One man among them wore a full-length robe, with a sapphire belt at his waist. They entered and stood beside the bronze altar.

Ezekiel 9:3.text: The glory of the God of Israel, which had been upon the cherubim, rose from them to the forecourt of the house. He called the man wearing the full-length robe, who had the belt at his waist,

Ezekiel 9:4.text: and said to him, “Pass through the midst of Jerusalem and put the sign upon the foreheads of the men who sigh deeply and grieve over all the lawlessness being committed within her.”

Ezekiel 9:5.text: To these others He said while I listened, “Go behind him into the city and strike. Do not spare with your eyes, and have no mercy.

Ezekiel 9:6.text: Old man, young man, maiden, infants and women—kill them to obliteration. But do not approach anyone upon whom the sign is. Begin at My holy places.” They began with the elderly men who were inside the house.

Ezekiel 9:7.text: He said to them, “Defile the house and fill the roads with the dead as you go out, and strike.”

Ezekiel 9:8.text: As they struck, I fall upon my face and cried aloud and said, “Alas, Lord! Art Thou obliterating the survivors of Israel as Thou pourest out Thy wrath upon Jerusalem?”

Ezekiel 9:9.text: He said to me, “The injustice of the house of Israel and Judah has grown very, very great, because the land is full of many peoples, and the city full of injustice and uncleanness. For they said, ‘The Lord has abandoned the land; the Lord does not look upon it.’

Ezekiel 9:10.text: My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy. I have brought their ways upon their heads.”

Ezekiel 9:11.text: And behold, the man wearing the full-length robe, with the belt fastened at his waist, answered, saying, “I have done as Thou didst command me.”

Ezekiel 10:1.text: I saw, and behold, above the firmament over the cherubim’s head was something like sapphire stone, a throne’s likeness above them.

Ezekiel 10:2.text: He said to the man wearing the robe, “Go in among the wheels beneath the cherubim, fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim, and scatter them over the city.” He went in before me.

Ezekiel 10:3.text: The cherubim stood to the right of the house as the man entered, and the cloud filled the inner court.

Ezekiel 10:4.text: The Lord’s glory departed from the cherubim to the forecourt of the house. The cloud filled the house, and the court filled with the radiance of the Lord’s glory.

Ezekiel 10:5.text: The sound of the cherubim’s wings was heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Shaddai speaking.

Ezekiel 10:6.text: When He commanded the man wearing the holy robe, saying, “Take fire from among the wheels, from among the cherubim,” he entered and stood beside the wheels,

Ezekiel 10:7.text: and he stretched out his hand into the midst of the fire among the cherubim, took it and gave it into the hands of the man wearing the holy robe. He took it and went out.

Ezekiel 10:8.text: I saw the cherubim, the likeness of human hands beneath their wings.

Ezekiel 10:9.text: I saw, and behold, four wheels stood beside the cherubim, one wheel beside one cherub. The wheels’ appearance was like the appearance of a carbuncle stone.

Ezekiel 10:10.text: Their appearance was one likeness for all four, as when a wheel is within a wheel.

Ezekiel 10:11.text: As they went, they went toward their four directions; they did not turn as they went. For wherever the one leading part looked, they went, and they did not turn as they went.

Ezekiel 10:12.text: Their backs, their hands, their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes all around, upon their four wheels.

Ezekiel 10:13.text: These wheels were called “Gelgel” in my hearing.

Ezekiel 10:15.text: The cherubim lifted themselves. This was the living creature I had seen at the river Chebar.

Ezekiel 10:16.text: When the cherubim went, the wheels went beside them. When the cherubim raised their wings to rise from the earth, their wheels did not turn.

Ezekiel 10:17.text: When they stood, these stood; when they rose, these rose with them, because a spirit of life was in them.

Ezekiel 10:18.text: The Lord’s glory went out from the house and mounted upon the cherubim,

Ezekiel 10:19.text: and the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth before me as they went out, with the wheels beside them. They stood at the entrance of the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.

Ezekiel 10:20.text: This is the living creature I had seen beneath the God of Israel at the river Chebar, and I knew that it was cherubim.

Ezekiel 10:21.text: Each had four faces, each had eight wings, and the likeness of human hands was beneath their wings.

Ezekiel 10:22.text: As for the likeness of their faces, these are the faces I had seen beneath the glory of the God of Israel at the river Chebar; each of them went straight ahead.

Ezekiel 11:1.text: A spirit lifted me and brought me to the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, facing east. And behold, at the gate entrance were about twenty-five men. Among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Ezer and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.

Ezekiel 11:2.text: The Lord said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who devise vain things and counsel wicked counsel in this city,

Ezekiel 11:3.text: who say, ‘Have the houses not been built recently? She is the cauldron, and we are the meat.’

Ezekiel 11:4.text: Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man.”

Ezekiel 11:5.text: The Lord’s spirit fell upon me, and He said to me, “Say, ‘Thus says the Lord: You have said this, house of Israel, and I understand the deliberations of your spirit.

Ezekiel 11:6.text: You have multiplied your dead in this city and filled her roads with the wounded.

Ezekiel 11:7.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Your dead whom you struck within her are the meat, and she is the cauldron; but I will bring you out of her.

Ezekiel 11:8.text: You fear the sword, and I will bring a sword upon you, says the Lord.

Ezekiel 11:9.text: I will bring you out of her midst, hand you into foreigners’ hands, and execute judgments among you.

Ezekiel 11:10.text: You will fall by the sword. At Israel’s borders I will judge you, and you will recognize that I am the Lord.

Ezekiel 11:11.text: She will not be a cauldron for you, and you certainly will not become meat within her. At Israel’s borders I will judge you,

Ezekiel 11:12.text: and you will recognize that I am the Lord.’”

Ezekiel 11:13.text: As I prophesied, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. I fall upon my face and cried aloud with a loud voice and said, “Alas, alas, Lord! Thou art bringing Israel’s survivors to a complete end!”

Ezekiel 11:14.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 11:15.text: “Son of man, your brothers and the men of your captivity and the whole house of Israel have been brought to an end. To them Jerusalem’s inhabitants said, ‘Keep far from the Lord; the land has been given to us as an inheritance.’

Ezekiel 11:16.text: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will thrust them away into the nations and scatter them through all the earth, and I will be a little sanctuary for them in the countries where they may enter.’

Ezekiel 11:17.text: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will receive them from the nations and gather them from the countries where I scattered them, and I will give them the land of Israel.

Ezekiel 11:18.text: They will enter there and remove all her abominations and all her lawlessness from her.

Ezekiel 11:19.text: I will give them another heart and put a new spirit within them. I will tear the stone heart from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,

Ezekiel 11:20.text: so that they may walk in My commands, keep My ordinances and carry them out. They will be My people, and I will be their God.

Ezekiel 11:21.text: As their heart went toward the heart of their abominations and their lawlessness, I have brought their ways upon their heads, says the Lord.’”

Ezekiel 11:22.text: The cherubim raised their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was upon them, above them.

Ezekiel 11:23.text: The Lord’s glory rose from the midst of the city and stood upon the mountain opposite the city.

Ezekiel 11:24.text: A spirit lifted me and brought me into the Chaldeans’ land, to the captives, in a vision by God’s spirit. I rose out of the vision I had seen,

Ezekiel 11:25.text: and I spoke to the captives all the Lord’s words that He had shown me.

Ezekiel 12:1.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 12:2.text: “Son of man, you dwell in the midst of their injustices. They have eyes to see and do not see, and ears to hear and do not hear, because they are an embittering house.

Ezekiel 12:3.text: And you, son of man, get your belongings ready for captivity by day before them. You will be taken captive from your place to another place before them, so that they may see, because they are an embittering house.

Ezekiel 12:4.text: You will bring your belongings out like belongings for captivity by day before their eyes, and you yourself will go out in the evening as a captive goes out.

Ezekiel 12:5.text: Before them, dig for yourself through the wall, and you will pass out through it.

Ezekiel 12:6.text: Before them you will be lifted upon shoulders and go out concealed. Cover your face, and you certainly will not see the land, for I have made you a portent to the house of Israel.”

Ezekiel 12:7.text: I did so according to all that He commanded me. I brought belongings out like belongings for captivity by day; in the evening I dug through the wall for myself and went out concealed. I was lifted upon shoulders before them.

Ezekiel 12:8.text: In the morning the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 12:9.text: “Son of man, has not the house of Israel, the embittering house, said to you, ‘What are you doing?’

Ezekiel 12:10.text: Say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: The ruler and the leader in Jerusalem and in the whole house of Israel, who are among them—’

Ezekiel 12:11.text: Say, ‘I perform portents in her midst. As I have done, so it will be for them; in deportation and captivity they will go.’

Ezekiel 12:12.text: The ruler among them will be lifted upon shoulders and go out concealed through the wall. He will dig through it to go out through it. He will cover his face so that he may not be seen by an eye, and he himself will not see the land.

Ezekiel 12:13.text: I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My enclosure. I will bring him to Babylon, to the Chaldeans’ land, and he will not see it, and there he will die.

Ezekiel 12:14.text: All those around him, his helpers and all who support him, I will scatter to every wind; I will draw a sword after them.

Ezekiel 12:15.text: They will know that I am the Lord when I scatter them among the nations, and I will disperse them among the countries.

Ezekiel 12:16.text: I will spare a few men among them from sword, famine and death, so that they may recount all their lawlessness among the nations where they entered, and they will know that I am the Lord.”

Ezekiel 12:17.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 12:18.text: “Son of man, eat your bread with pain, and drink your water with torment and distress,

Ezekiel 12:19.text: and say to the people of the land, ‘Thus says the Lord to Jerusalem’s inhabitants upon Israel’s land: They will eat their bread with want and drink their water with devastation, so that the land may be destroyed with its fullness, for all who dwell in it are in impiety.

Ezekiel 12:20.text: Their inhabited cities will be made desolate, and the land will be laid waste. You will recognize that I am the Lord.’”

Ezekiel 12:21.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 12:22.text: “Son of man, what is this proverb you have concerning Israel’s land, saying, ‘The days are far off; vision has perished’?

Ezekiel 12:23.text: Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will turn back this proverb, and the house of Israel certainly will no longer say this proverb.’ For you will speak to them: ‘The days have drawn near, and the word of every vision,

Ezekiel 12:24.text: because there will no longer be any false vision or anyone divining pleasing things among the sons of Israel,

Ezekiel 12:25.text: because I, the Lord, will speak My words; I will speak and act, and I certainly will delay no longer. For in your days, embittering house, I will speak a word and act, says the Lord.’”

Ezekiel 12:26.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 12:27.text: “Son of man, behold, the embittering house of Israel keeps saying, ‘The vision this man sees is for many days ahead; this man prophesies of times far ahead.’

Ezekiel 12:28.text: Therefore say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: None of My words that I may speak will be prolonged any longer. I will speak and act, says the Lord.’”

Ezekiel 13:1.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 13:2.text: “Son of man, prophesy against Israel’s prophets; you will prophesy and say to them, ‘Hear the Lord’s word!

Ezekiel 13:3.text: Thus says the Lord: Woe to those who prophesy from their own heart and see nothing at all!

Ezekiel 13:4.text: Your prophets, Israel, are like foxes in the wildernesses.

Ezekiel 13:5.text: They did not stand in a firm position, and they gathered flocks against the house of Israel. Those saying, ‘On the Lord’s day,’ did not rise.

Ezekiel 13:6.text: They see false things and divine vain things, those who say, ‘The Lord says,’ although the Lord has not sent them; and they began to establish a word.

Ezekiel 13:7.text: Have you not seen a false vision and spoken vain divinations?

Ezekiel 13:8.text: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because your words are false and your divinations vain, therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord,

Ezekiel 13:9.text: and I will stretch out My hand against the prophets who see false things and utter vain things. They will not belong to My people’s instruction, nor be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor enter Israel’s land. They will know that I am the Lord.

Ezekiel 13:10.text: Because they misled My people, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there was no peace, and this one builds a wall, and they coat it—if it is going to fall,

Ezekiel 13:11.text: say to those coating it, ‘It will fall.’ There will be a flooding downpour, and I will put stones for hurling into their bonds, and they will fall; there will be an upending wind, and it will be split.

Ezekiel 13:12.text: And behold, the wall has fallen! Will they not say to you, ‘Where is your coating with which you coated it?’

Ezekiel 13:13.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: I will unleash an upending blast with wrath; a flooding downpour will come in My anger, and I will bring the projectile stones in wrath for complete destruction,

Ezekiel 13:14.text: and I will tear down the wall you coated, and it will fall. I will lay it upon the ground; its foundations will be uncovered, and it will fall, and you will be brought to an end with rebukes. You will recognize that I am the Lord.

Ezekiel 13:15.text: I will complete My wrath upon the wall and those coating it, and it will fall. I said to you, ‘There is no wall, nor those coating it—

Ezekiel 13:16.text: the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem and see peace for her, when there is no peace,’ says the Lord.’

Ezekiel 13:17.text: And you, son of man, set your face firmly against the daughters of your people who prophesy from their own heart, and prophesy against them,

Ezekiel 13:18.text: and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Woe to the women sewing cushions upon every elbow of an arm and making coverings upon every head of every age, to distort lives! The lives of My people were distorted, and they were preserving lives.

Ezekiel 13:19.text: They were profaning Me among My people for a handful of barley and scraps of bread, putting to death lives that ought not die and preserving lives that ought not live, as you uttered things to a people listening to vain pronouncements.

Ezekiel 13:20.text: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against your cushions, on which you entangle lives. I will tear them from your arms and send the lives out—their lives that you twist away—into dispersion.

Ezekiel 13:21.text: I will tear your coverings and rescue My people from your hand. They will no longer be in your hands for entanglement, and you will recognize that I am the Lord.

Ezekiel 13:22.text: Because you distorted the righteous person’s heart unjustly, though I was not distorting him, and strengthened the lawless person’s hands so that he does not turn at all from his evil way and live,

Ezekiel 13:23.text: therefore you certainly will no longer see false things or divine divinations. I will rescue My people from your hand, and you will know that I am the Lord.’”

Ezekiel 14:1.text: Men from Israel’s elders came to me and sat before me.

Ezekiel 14:2.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 14:3.text: “Son of man, these men have set their thoughts upon their hearts and set the punishment of their injustices before their faces. Shall I indeed answer them?

Ezekiel 14:4.text: Therefore speak to them and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Anyone of the house of Israel who sets his thoughts upon his heart, places the punishment of his injustice before his face, and comes to the prophet—I, the Lord, will answer him in the things in which his mind is entangled,

Ezekiel 14:5.text: so that it may turn the house of Israel aside in accordance with their hearts, alienated from Me through their reflections.’

Ezekiel 14:6.text: Therefore say to the house of Israel, ‘Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Turn back and turn away from your practices and all your impieties, and turn your faces.

Ezekiel 14:7.text: For anyone of the house of Israel or of the sojourners living among Israel who becomes alienated from Me, sets his reflections upon his heart, places the punishment of his injustice before his face, and comes to the prophet to question him concerning Me—I, the Lord, will answer him in that in which he is entangled.

Ezekiel 14:8.text: I will set My face firmly against that person, make him a wilderness and a devastation, and remove him from the midst of My people. You will recognize that I am the Lord.

Ezekiel 14:9.text: If the prophet is led astray and speaks, I, the Lord, have led that prophet astray. I will stretch out My hand against him and destroy him from the midst of My people Israel.

Ezekiel 14:10.text: They will receive their injustice; according to the inquirer’s offense and according to the offense, it will likewise be for the prophet,

Ezekiel 14:11.text: so that the house of Israel may no longer wander from Me or be defiled by any of their transgressions. They will be My people, and I will be their God, says the Lord.’”

Ezekiel 14:12.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 14:13.text: “Son of man, if a land sins against Me by committing a transgression, and I stretch My hand against it, shatter its support of bread, send famine upon it, and remove human and livestock from it,

Ezekiel 14:14.text: even if these three men—Noah, Daniel and Job—were within it, they themselves would be saved by their righteousness, says the Lord.

Ezekiel 14:15.text: Even if I bring evil beasts upon the land and punish it, so that it becomes a devastation and no one passes through because of the beasts,

Ezekiel 14:16.text: and these three men were within it, as I live, says the Lord, neither sons nor daughters would be saved; only they themselves would be saved, and the land would be destroyed.

Ezekiel 14:17.text: Or even if I bring a sword upon that land and say, ‘Let a sword pass through the land,’ and remove human and livestock from it,

Ezekiel 14:18.text: and these three men were within it, as I live, says the Lord, they certainly would not rescue sons or daughters; they alone would be saved.

Ezekiel 14:19.text: Or even if I send death upon that land and pour My wrath upon it in blood, to destroy human and livestock from it,

Ezekiel 14:20.text: and Noah, Daniel and Job were within it, as I live, says the Lord, neither sons nor daughters would be left; they would rescue their own lives by their righteousness.

Ezekiel 14:21.text: Thus says the Lord: Even if I send My four evil retributions—sword, famine, evil beasts and death—against Jerusalem, to destroy human and livestock from her,

Ezekiel 14:22.text: and behold, her rescued survivors are left in her, bringing sons and daughters out of her. Behold, they are coming out to you. You will see their ways and their reflections and feel regret over the evils I brought upon Jerusalem—all the evils I brought upon her,

Ezekiel 14:23.text: and they will comfort you, because you will see their ways and their reflections, and recognize that I have not done in vain all that I did in her, says the Lord.”

Ezekiel 15:1.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 15:2.text: “And you, son of man, what could vinewood be among all the branch wood found among the forest trees?

Ezekiel 15:3.text: Will they take wood from it to make anything useful? Will they take a peg from it to hang any vessel upon it?

Ezekiel 15:4.text: It has only been given to the fire to be consumed. Fire consumes its yearly prunings, and it is utterly spent. Surely it will not be useful for work?

Ezekiel 15:5.text: Even when it is whole, it will not serve for work. How much less if fire consumes it completely—will it still serve for work?

Ezekiel 15:6.text: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: As with the vinewood among the forest trees, which I have given to the fire to be consumed, so I have given Jerusalem’s inhabitants.

Ezekiel 15:7.text: I will set My face against them. They will come out of the fire, and fire will devour them. They will recognize that I am the Lord when I set My face firmly against them.

Ezekiel 15:8.text: I will lay the land waste, because they have fallen into transgression, says the Lord.’”

Ezekiel 16:1.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 16:2.text: “Son of man, solemnly testify to Jerusalem about her lawlessness,

Ezekiel 16:3.text: and say, ‘Thus says the Lord to Jerusalem: Your root and your birth are from the land of Canaan; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.

Ezekiel 16:4.text: As for your birth, on the day you were born they did not bind your breasts; you were not washed with water, not salted with salt, and not wrapped in swaddling cloths.

Ezekiel 16:5.text: Nor did My eye spare you to do any of all these things for you, to feel anything for you. You were cast upon the face of the plain because of your life’s crookedness, on the day you were born.

Ezekiel 16:6.text: I passed by you and saw you befouled in your blood, and said to you, ‘From your blood, life!

Ezekiel 16:7.text: Multiply!’ I have made you like the growth of the field. You multiplied, grew great and entered cities of cities. Your breasts stood firm and your hair grew, but you were naked and exposed.

Ezekiel 16:8.text: I passed through you and saw you; behold, your season was the season of those lodging. I spread My wings over you and covered your exposure. I swore to you and entered a covenant with you, says the Lord, and you became Mine.

Ezekiel 16:9.text: I washed you with water, washed your blood off you, and anointed you with oil,

Ezekiel 16:10.text: and clothed you in patterned garments, gave you blue-purple footwear, girded you with fine linen, and wrapped you in hair-woven cloth,

Ezekiel 16:11.text: and adorned you with ornaments, placed bracelets around your hands and a necklace around your neck,

Ezekiel 16:12.text: and put a ring around your nostril, little hoops upon your ears and a crown of boasting upon your head.

Ezekiel 16:13.text: You were adorned with gold and silver; your coverings were fine linen, hair-woven and patterned. You ate fine flour, oil and honey, and became very beautiful.

Ezekiel 16:14.text: Your fame went out among the nations because of your beauty, for it was made complete in splendor, in the loveliness I placed upon you, says the Lord.

Ezekiel 16:15.text: You trusted in your beauty and prostituted yourself because of your fame. You poured out your prostitution upon every passerby—which will not be.

Ezekiel 16:16.text: You took some of your garments, made sewn idols for yourself and prostituted yourself upon them. You certainly will not enter, nor will it come to be.

Ezekiel 16:17.text: You took your vessels of boasting from My gold and My silver, from what I had given you, made male images for yourself and prostituted yourself among them.

Ezekiel 16:18.text: You took your patterned clothing and clothed them; you set My oil and My incense before them.

Ezekiel 16:19.text: My loaves that I gave you—fine flour, oil and honey with which I fed you—you set before them as a fragrant aroma. So it happened, says the Lord.

Ezekiel 16:20.text: You took your sons and daughters whom you had borne and sacrificed them to them for consumption, as though you had prostituted yourself only a little,

Ezekiel 16:21.text: and slaughtered your children and gave them over as you used them for averting rites.

Ezekiel 16:22.text: This was in addition to all your prostitution, and you did not remember the days of your infancy, when you were naked and exposed and lived befouled in your blood.

Ezekiel 16:23.text: After all your evils, says the Lord,

Ezekiel 16:24.text: you built yourself a prostitution chamber and made yourself a display place in every broad street,

Ezekiel 16:25.text: and at the head of every road you built your brothels, ruined your beauty, spread your legs to every passerby, and multiplied your prostitution.

Ezekiel 16:26.text: You prostituted yourself with the sons of Egypt, your neighbors great in flesh, and prostituted yourself in many ways to anger Me.

Ezekiel 16:27.text: But if I stretch My hand against you, I will remove your ordinances and hand you over to the desires of those who hate you, daughters of foreigners who turn you aside from your way in which you acted impiously.

Ezekiel 16:28.text: You prostituted yourself with the daughters of Assyria, and not even so were you filled; you prostituted yourself, and were not filled.

Ezekiel 16:29.text: You multiplied your covenants toward the Chaldeans’ land, and not even with these were you filled.

Ezekiel 16:30.text: What shall I do to your daughter, says the Lord, when you do all these things, the works of a prostitute? And you prostituted yourself threefold

Ezekiel 16:31.text: among your daughters. You built your brothel at every road head and made your platform in every broad street, and became like a prostitute gathering payments.

Ezekiel 16:32.text: The adulterous wife is like you, receiving payments from her husband;

Ezekiel 16:33.text: she kept giving payments to all who prostituted her. You too gave payments to all your lovers and loaded them up to come to you from all around in your prostitution.

Ezekiel 16:34.text: With you it became distorted compared with other women in your prostitution. They have prostituted themselves with you as you paid extra payments, and no payments were given to you; with you things became distorted.

Ezekiel 16:35.text: Therefore, prostitute, hear the Lord’s word!

Ezekiel 16:36.text: Thus says the Lord: Because you poured out your copper, your shame will be exposed in your prostitution with your lovers, in all the reflections of your lawlessness, and in the blood of your children whom you gave to them.
